## Natural history notes

A large scoliid wasp characterized by a black body with pale yellow to whitish markings and noticeably hairy, feather-like hind legs. In Florida, the Feather-legged Scoliid Wasp is found in sandy open habitats such as scrub, sandhills, pine flatwoods, fields, roadsides, gardens, and forest edges where flowers and soil-dwelling beetle larvae occur. Adults visit flowers for nectar, while females dig into the soil to find scarab beetle grubs, paralyzing them and laying an egg so the wasp larva can develop as a parasitoid.
